adjudications.why: Register-level defect, not a book defect. (a) The block labelled 'common_all_8' lists only 2 of 4 models per entry, which contradicts the convergence framing (4/4) and the prompt's §1 'agreement upgrades COVERAGE, never SEVERITY'. Either the label or the models field is wrong; until reconciled, no 'common' entry may be cited as convergent. (b) Ids collide across models: CH4-01, CH2-01, CH26-01, FIG-26.2-01 and FIG-3.4-01 each appear twice with different content (MiMo's FIG-3.4-01 is a legend text collision; MiniMax's is a 4-of-8-cells-shaded defect). (c) The 's' field mixes quoted clause with defect statement and truncates mid-sentence in ~20 entries, so most entries cannot be adjudicated on their merits. (d) No artifact lock (PDF SHA-256, page count, printed-page offset) is recorded anywhere in the register, although §0 requires it; the printed offset of 20 is inferable only from PAGE-339-340-DUP-01 and FIG-2.2-01.

The quoted content is a parenthetical, not a defect statement, and its truth is precision-dependent: 70B at FP16 = 140 GB does NOT fit on one 80 GB H100, so 'weights alone fit on 1×H100' is false under FP16; under FP8 (70 GB) it fits with ~10 GB left, which is not '7 GPUs free' in the sense the parenthetical implies. Acceptance test: state the canonical precision and per-GPU weight bytes, then reconcile with the 436 GB pool (Ch 7) and the 24.1/24.9 GB per-request KV figures (Ch 11/Ch 7).

As a precision defect the quoted clause is genuinely weak: 'arithmetic intensity' is a ratio, not a cost, so 'the dominant cost ... is the arithmetic intensity' names a property of the workload where it should name a resource (FLOP/s or bytes/s). 'Dominant' is also an unqualified universal. Fix: name the two resources and scope the claim to the regimes established in Ch 6/8. Severity P3 as filed is appropriate.

Legitimate under §38 only if the four items are researchable-now. The four legitimate uncertainty categories are: empirical data unavailable, workload-dependent, implementation-dependent, technology evolving. 'Unresolved (evidence pending)' is not one of them. Acceptance test: list the four items and classify each; any item that is merely 'not yet checked' must be resolved before publication rather than deferred.

The quoted numbers are defensible and should not be filed as errors: NDR 400 Gb/s with 64b/66b encoding gives ~388 Gb/s payload (~380 is right), and 200 Gb/s RoCEv2 gives ~180–195 Gb/s depending on MTU and header overhead. If the finding is that these numbers are wrong, it is a false positive; if the finding is that the ~5–10% gap is silently applied to a per-second throughput computation, that is a scope/derivation issue and needs the specific downstream substitution quoted.

A benign reading is available and is probably the intended one: PagedAttention's contribution is eliminating fragmentation, so 'the ~24.1 GB-per-request KV pack fits' can be true in the fragmentation sense (a 24.1 GB contiguous block would not fit in a fragmented pool, but 24.1 GB of free pages does). The finding is valid only if the text attributes a reduction in KV SIZE to paging. Acceptance test: check whether the sentence claims size reduction; if not, the fix is a one-clause clarification ('fits as non-contiguous pages, not as a contiguous block'), not a rewrite. Note the 24.1 GB figure itself is correct and cross-consistent: 2 × 80 × 9,200 × 8,192 × 2 B = 24.1 GB.

The quoted sentence is a self-deprecating editorial aside about the book's own Chapter 22 ('an abstract meta-method ... that does not instantiate against concrete substrate constraints'). This is a real defect: it disparages a chapter the book asks the reader to trust, and it creates a dangling promise — if Ch 22 is abstract and non-instantiating, its presence in the book needs justification. Fix: replace the meta-commentary with a substantive contrast (what Ch 22 abstracts over that Ch 12 instantiates against real substrate numbers).

The arithmetic is internally consistent and should not be the basis of the finding: 10 × 8.6 = 86 in-flight (Little's law); 86 × 27.2 GB = 2.34 TB; 27.2 GB / 10,365 tokens = 2.62 MB/token, matching the canonical FP16 KV constant. Two open questions the finding does not settle: (a) whether W_exec = 8.6 s is end-to-end response time INCLUDING queueing — if so, the 86 in-flight includes queued requests, which do not hold KV, so 86 × 27.2 GB overstates KV residency; (b) whether 2.3 TB is reconciled against fleet KV capacity (21 hosts × 8 × 80 GB = 13.4 TB minus ~1.5 TB weights). Acceptance test: state whether 8.6 s is service or response time and compute residency over running requests only.

120 ms per agent turn against the canonical TPOT of ~25 ms (Ch 2) is a 4.8× gap that requires decomposition: re-prefill of the growing context (10,000 tokens ÷ 19,780 tok/s ≈ 0.51 s if uncached), attention over the 10K context, and TP all-reduce. If 120 ms is a per-turn TOTAL including prefill, the label 'per-turn agent step' is acceptable but must say so; if it is claimed as a decode step, it contradicts Ch 2. Acceptance test: state the components of the 120 ms.

Derivable from the book's own numbers: 9,200 tokens ÷ 19,780 tok/s = 0.465 s, so a 1.08 s prefill implies ~8,520 tok/s = 43% of the Ch 8/Ch 20 ceiling, i.e. ~15% MFU against the stated 35%. The 1.08 s value is used downstream (the 1.2 s TTFT budget), so the rounding-tolerance exemption does not apply. Benign reading: 1.08 s may be TTFT including queueing rather than pure prefill — in which case the defect is mis-attribution rather than arithmetic, and the fix is to label it. Acceptance test: state whether 1.08 s is prefill-only or TTFT; if prefill-only, reconcile with 19,780 tok/s or state the different MFU/host count.

Denominator/population mismatch in the finding itself. 40 × 1.29 = 51.6 PFLOP/s is FLEET-WIDE demand at the 40 rps peak; 8 × 0.989 = 7.91 PFLOPS is ONE host's dense peak. The two sides are not comparable. Correct comparisons from the book's own numbers: fleet-wide 51.6 PFLOP/s vs 21 hosts × 2.77 PFLOPS (35% MFU) ≈ 58 PFLOPS → ρ ≈ 0.89; or per-host (40/21 ≈ 1.9 rps) × 1.29 = 2.45 PFLOP/s vs 2.77 PFLOPS → ρ ≈ 0.89. Both are consistent with the canonical fleet sizing, so the 6.5× figure is an artifact of mixing populations. Re-file only if Ch 6 itself prints this comparison.

The quoted cell list (29/32/34/82/205/410) carries no stated defect. The likely issue, given CH19-01, is that the agentic columns omit the α amplification from Ch 4 (cumulative-context total vs single-shot equivalent) — note 410/205 = 2 and 82/34 ≈ 2.4, i.e. the columns appear to be per-call rather than cumulative. Acceptance test: recompute each cell from the canonical per-call token counts and α, and state whether the no-reuse FP8 column is scaled.

The quoted clause is a definition, not a defect. The risk is downstream: if Ch 17/19 tables use per-call rather than cumulative-context totals, the α factor is defined but not applied. Acceptance test: verify every agentic token total in Ch 17 and Ch 19 is the cumulative-context total, and that α is stated numerically at each point of use rather than only in Ch 4.

The quoted clause appears to be the book's own disclaimer ('reference points, not measured clusters'), so the defect, if any, is that the archetype table is presented with the same visual authority and typography as measured data elsewhere in the chapter. Acceptance test: check the table's evidence labels against the Ch 4 / Appendix A three-axis taxonomy (provenance × status × analytical) and confirm the disclaimer is attached to the table, not only to the surrounding prose.

Same-line glyph overlap is the declared scope of render/scan_overlaps.py; per house convention §9 a gate hit is reportable only if the gate's SCOPE is wrong. The finding implies the gate does not cover figure text. Acceptance test: run the gate over figure text; if it does not cover it, extend the gate and re-run rather than carrying this as a reviewer finding.

The underlying inconsistency is real (two per-engineer cost figures in one mini-case) but the stated magnitude is not reproducible from the quoted fragments. On the natural reading, 0.5 FTE at $26K/mo = $52K/yr for 0.5 FTE = $104K/yr per FTE, versus '$62K/yr fully loaded for one engineer' = $62K/yr per FTE → 1.7×, not ~10×. If $26K/mo is quoted per FTE, 0.5 FTE = $156K/yr → 2.5×. If $62K/yr is a whole-team figure, the ratio is 5×. Acceptance test: re-quote both expressions with their units and reconcile to one per-FTE fully loaded figure; correct the finding's factor to whatever the text actually supports.

A duplicated page body would be a serious production defect, but it is trivially machine-detectable and should be a gate, not a reviewer finding. The printed offset of 20 (PDF 359 → printed 339) is consistent with the house convention, which is a point in the finding's favour. Acceptance test: extract and diff the text of PDF pages 359 and 360; if identical, fix the LaTeX float/page-break and add a duplicate-page detector to the gates.

The substance is correct at the stated operating point — static batching of 10 × 9.2K = 92K tokens takes ~4.65 s to first token, far above the 1.2 s TTFT budget — but 'nearly mandatory' is a modal necessity claim of exactly the kind §6 flags. It must be scoped to (single host, 10 rps, 9.2K prefill, 1.2 s TTFT) and should name the alternatives (chunked prefill, more hosts, smaller model, disaggregation). Severity P1 is inflated: no architecture decision is wrong once the condition is stated. P2.

Real terminology defect, wrong severity. 'Higher-bandwidth memory topologies (NVSwitch, HBM3e)' conflates three layers: NVSwitch is an interconnect fabric, HBM3e is a memory standard, and only 'larger NVLink domains' is a topology. Fix the taxonomy; no architecture decision changes. P2/P3, not P1.

The roofline geometry is checkable from the book's own numbers: ridge = 989e12 ÷ 3.35e12 = 295 FLOP/byte, so the memory-bound line must pass through (AI = 1, 3.35e12) and (AI = 295, 9.9e14). A segment starting at ~1e12 at AI = 1 implies a ridge at ~1000, contradicting the labelled ~295. Acceptance test: verify the drawn line passes through those two points and that the ridge label sits at the intersection.

The figure asserts as FACT the three quantities the facing prose says are assumed. This is a label misapplication under the book's own taxonomy (Ch 4 / Appendix A axis table), and it sits in the capstone's headline evidence box, so it is the most consequential instance of this class. Fix: relabel the box as ASSUMPTION/ILLUSTRATIVE, or restate the prose so the box is true. Note the internal tension with CH26-01 (MiniMax): the box says utilization 45% while the prose implies ρ ≈ 1 against a ~2.0 req/s ceiling — the operating point must be reconciled.

The quoted annotation 'crossover ~106.8K' is arithmetically CORRECT for the causal-triangle crossover: L* = 2N ÷ (160·d) = 1.4e11 ÷ (160 × 8,192) = 106,800 tokens. The truncated complaint ('a total curve (linear + half quadratic) is a…') cannot be evaluated without the full sentence. Acceptance test: state what the green series' crossover is DEFINED as (attention = linear, or attention = 50% of total) and check the label matches the definition.

The quoted cell 'MoE (8×7B class)' carries no stated defect. The checkable tension is with Fig 3.4: 8 × 7B at FP16 = 112 GB, while the figure shows ~94 GB MoE resident — reconcile parameter count, precision, and any shared/dense components, or state that the figure's MoE is not the 8×7B class.

The table's own arithmetic is right (92,000 ÷ 24,725 = 3.72 → 4 hosts) but the DENOMINATOR conflicts with the book's canonical per-host prefill ceiling of 19,780 tok/s (Ch 8 and Ch 20: 8 × 0.989 PF/s × 35% ÷ 2 × 70e9). 24,725 = 19,780 × 1.25 exactly, so a 25% discrepancy sits inside a host-count decision. Acceptance test: locate the derivation of 24,725; if it uses a different MFU or FLOP convention, state it in the table; otherwise correct to 19,780, which gives 92,000 ÷ 19,780 = 4.65 → 5 hosts.

Cross-reference correctness depends on the actual chapter titles, which are not in the register. Independently of that, the quoted clause merges two distinct triggers under one 'required when': (a) model exceeds node memory → sharding, (b) traffic exceeds one host → P/D disaggregation. These have different preconditions and different remedies and should be separate clauses. Acceptance test: verify the Ch 10 and Ch 11 titles and that each trigger points at the chapter that actually covers it.

1 ÷ 0.07 = 14.3× is arithmetically right, but the framing ('the constant factor itself can be cut ~10–14×') attaches a KV-SIZE reduction to a general 'constant factor', inviting the reader to infer a FLOP reduction. KV bytes and FLOPs are different resources and must not share a factor. Acceptance test: state, per variant, WHICH resource the 10–14× applies to, and keep each endpoint tied to a named variant and a named mechanism (e.g. attention re-architecture → KV bytes only).

The quote is truncated mid-clause, so the defect cannot be identified. The checkable requirement is whether pattern selection is driven by explicit criteria (workload shape, SLO, diagnosed bottleneck) rather than by a catalogue lookup. Acceptance test: re-quote in full and check for a stated decision rule with an ordering.

Self-evident arithmetic/direction error: 0.2K = 200 FLOP/byte < 295, so 'well to the right of the ~295 ridge' is false on its own terms (200 is on the memory-bound side). Worse, the canonical prefill arithmetic intensity is ≈ L FLOP/byte ≈ 9,200 (2NL FLOPs over 2N weight bytes), which is ~46× the caption's 0.2K and ~224× the caption's 41 (see FIG-2.2-A). Three mutually inconsistent values on one page. Acceptance test: one number, one marker, one direction, with the formula stated in the caption.

Same root cause as FIG-26.2-01 (DeepSeek) and FIG-26.2-02 (MiniMax) — ONE root cause, three anchors: the '1 · FACT' box asserts as FACT the three quantities the prose says are assumed. Also note the unresolved operating-point tension: the box says utilization 45% while CH26-01 (MiniMax) reasons from ρ ≈ 1 against a ~2.0 req/s ceiling. Reconcile before fixing the labels.

Clean, self-contained, high-value: 'problem: TTFT p95 2.1 s' with 'success criterion: p5 TTFT ≤ 2 s' is a trivially satisfiable criterion, since p5 ≤ p95 = 2.1 s holds by construction and p5 is typically far below 2 s. The criterion must be p95 ≤ 2 s (or p99). A wrong SLO in a capstone lets a failing design pass its own gate. Acceptance test: the criterion's percentile must match the problem's percentile.

The arithmetic checks out (331.2M input tokens/h ÷ $120/h = 2.76M tokens per dollar; 90K output tokens/$ implies ~300 output tokens/request at 10 rps), so the finding is not about the arithmetic. The open question is the BASIS: ~6 hosts average vs the canonical 21/22 hosts (Ch 20), and the monthly volume basis — 10 rps × 2,592,000 s = 25.92M req/mo, whereas 6.24M req/mo corresponds to ~2.4 rps (a 4.15× difference). Acceptance test: state the host count and the rps behind $120/h and reconcile with Ch 16 and Ch 20.

140 GB ÷ 0.025 s = 5.6 TB/s is arithmetically correct, but it is a whole-model batch-1-equivalent requirement. On 8×H100 the aggregate HBM bandwidth is 26.8 TB/s and the per-GPU requirement is 700 GB/s against 3.35 TB/s available, so the requirement is comfortably met at TP=8; a single H100 would need 41.8 ms per step. The finding is valid only if the table presents 5.6 TB/s beside a single H100's 3.35 TB/s without stating the TP basis. Acceptance test: label the row with device count and per-GPU vs aggregate basis.

The recommendation is self-defeating as quoted: prefix/RadixAttention caching is enabled BECAUSE the hit rate is low, but a low hit rate is precisely the condition under which prefix caching returns little. The correct response to a low hit rate is to reduce prefix diversity, shorten the shared prefix, or accept the prefill cost. Acceptance test: the decision must follow from the measured hit rate and the prefix-length distribution, not from the mere presence of a low hit rate.

Same root cause as CH4-01 (DeepSeek): 'near-mandatory' is a modal necessity claim. Scope it to the stated operating point (single host, 10 rps, 9.2K prefill, 1.2 s TTFT) and name the alternatives. Severity P2, not P1.

Re-file of an explicitly rejected Round-1 class ('CH18/CH19-02/CH20-01 benign readings confirmed at source'). The arithmetic is correct: 8 × 0.989e15 × 0.35 ÷ (2 × 70e9) = 19,779 tokens/s, and the convention is stated (35% MFU, prefill-only, linear-only FLOP). Re-file only with new primary evidence.

Re-file of an explicitly rejected Round-1 class ('CH19-02 benign reading confirmed at source'). The substance quoted — a fallback occupying the top 2% of the distribution leaves the unconditional p95 equal to the conditional p95 — is a correct statement of percentile behaviour, not a defect. Re-file only with new primary evidence.

The KV arithmetic is correct and is a useful cross-check: 2 × 80 × 9,200 × 8,192 × 2 B = 24.1 GB, matching Ch 11's 24.1 GB exactly. The open question is the '≈ 30 GB' activation figure, which needs an explicit decomposition: hidden state 9,200 × 8,192 × 2 B = 151 MB; MLP intermediates ~0.6–1.8 GB; logits 9,200 × 128K × 2 B = 2.4 GB (4.7 GB FP32). 30 GB is not reachable from those without a stated cause, and it must be labelled per-host or per-TP-rank. Acceptance test: itemize the 30 GB and state the sharding.

A 450 ms service-time sum with no queueing term cannot support a p99 TTFT claim at ρ ≈ 1: as ρ → 1 the queueing delay diverges, so the p99 is unbounded under the stated model. This is a methodological defect in the capstone's headline number, and it interacts with the 'utilization 45%' claim in the same figure (see F-26.2-1). Acceptance test: either add the queueing term at the stated ρ, or restate the claim explicitly as a service-time floor.

The quote is truncated. The checkable requirement is whether each Patterns Library entry carries decision criteria (trigger condition, precondition, expected effect, failure mode, cost) or is merely descriptive. Acceptance test: re-quote in full and check for a 'when to use / when not to use' field per pattern.

The finding lists model families in A.3–A.5 and A.10 'First-hand Sources' but never states the defect. The checkable questions are (a) whether each A.3–A.5 entry has a matching A.10 first-party citation, and (b) whether a model card or vendor release page is being cited as a first-party source for a performance number it does not contain. Acceptance test: for each of the five families, confirm a first-party URL and that the cited number appears in it.

Three mutually inconsistent prefill arithmetic intensities on one page: caption ~41 FLOP/byte, plotted marker ~10^4, prose ~2K. The book's own numbers give ≈ L FLOP/byte ≈ 9,200 for a 9.2K-token prefill (2NL FLOPs over 2N weight bytes), so the plotted marker is right and both the caption's 41 and the prose's 2K are wrong (by ~224× and ~4.6× respectively). Acceptance test: one value, one marker, and the caption must state the formula (2NL ÷ 2N bytes = L).

Same root cause as FIG-2.2-01 (DeepSeek) — ONE root cause, two anchors: the drawn ridge must sit at 295 FLOP/byte and the memory-bound line must pass through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 9.9e14). The decode marker must sit near AI ≈ 1 (batch-1 decode AI ≈ 2N FLOPs ÷ 2N weight bytes ≈ 1 FLOP/byte), far left of the ridge.

Well-formed: an 'initialize' arrow terminating at the RIGHT end of the DECODE band breaks the loop's reading order, since the reader's eye must enter at 'previous token'. Acceptance test: the arrow must terminate at the loop's entry point, and the entry point must be the leftmost element of the band.

Well-formed and mechanistically the highest-value figure check in the register: if the figure appends a token's K/V on the same step the token is sampled, it teaches the wrong autoregressive semantics (the sampled token's K/V is produced by the NEXT forward pass). This is precisely the misconception class §48 names. Acceptance test: the append arrow must originate from the forward pass that consumes the previous token, and the caption must state that the cache holds K/V for all PRIOR tokens.

Well-formed: four of eight cells shaded 'active' contradicts a 'top-2 active' panel label and the legend, and it breaks the book's own ratio (94 GB resident ÷ 4 = 23.5 GB active, i.e. top-2 of 8). Acceptance test: exactly two cells shaded, or relabel the panel and the legend.

The quoted totals are mutually consistent (94 GB resident, ~23 GB active; 94/4 = 23.5), so the alleged caption/figure mismatch must live in the caption's per-component decomposition, which is not quoted. Acceptance test: re-quote the caption's decomposition and check that it sums to 94 GB and that the active figure sums to 23.5 GB; also reconcile 94 GB against 8 × 7B FP16 = 112 GB (see CH3-T3-01).

Well-formed arrow-direction defect; the caption and the figure's inline key are the oracle and must agree with the rendered arrowheads. Acceptance test: arrowheads must match the key for both vertical arrows.

Misread of the render. The same box is quoted independently by DeepSeek as containing 'baseline TTFT p99 450 ms', so the token is 'p99', not '099'; the 'p' is most likely clipped or overlapped by the box edge. Residual, if any: a clipped 'p' is a P3 rendering fix, not a P1 stray-number defect. (Also note the id collision with DeepSeek's FIG-26.2-01.)

Same root cause as FIG-26.2-01 (DeepSeek) and F-26.2-1 (Qwen): ONE root cause, three anchors — the '1 · FACT' box asserts as FACT the three quantities the prose says are assumed. Fix once, at the box, and re-check the prose's parallel claims.

Well-formed control-flow defect: a solid (executed) arrow originating from a dashed node explicitly labelled 'not executed' teaches the wrong control flow. Acceptance test: the 'exit after pass 2' arrow must originate from the pass-2 node.

The quote is truncated to 'Scope: FP16', so the incoherence cannot be located. The checkable requirement is that a Scope sentence must state precision, batch/concurrency, and regime (prefill vs decode), and must agree with the legend and the in-figure annotations. Acceptance test: re-quote in full and check all three fields.

The displayed substitution '≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests' uses '+' where the result requires '÷': 436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51 ✓. The result is right, the operator is wrong, and the line is a displayed derivation a reader will copy. Severity P1, not P0. Two checks the finding does not make: (a) 436 GB must be NET of resident weights (8 × 80 = 640 GB physical; 140 GB FP16 weights → 500 GB; 436 GB implies a further 64 GB reserve) or the 17-request figure double-counts weights; (b) the per-request KV figure must be reconciled with 24.1 GB (Ch 11) and 27.2 GB (Ch 19) — 24.9 GB implies ~9,504 tokens at 2.62 MB/token, not the canonical 9,200.

Re-file of an explicitly rejected Round-1 class ('FIG-8.2-1 "989 sparse" (datasheet: dense)'), and the house convention fixes H100 FP16 dense = 989 TFLOPS (1,979 with sparsity; FP8 dense = 1,979). The filed evidence is a render-based 'the drawing shows bo…' contradiction, not a primary-source derivation. If the residual claim is that the caption pairs 1,979 with H200 as a dense figure, re-file it with the NVIDIA datasheets: H200 SXM is FP16 dense 989 TFLOPS / sparsity 1,979, and differs from H100 in HBM bandwidth (4.8 TB/s), not tensor throughput.

The quoted fragment is self-contradictory as written ('decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the compute-bound side; decode (batch=1) …'), and the physics is unambiguous: at batch 1 the decode arithmetic intensity is ≈ 1 FLOP/byte (2N FLOPs over 2N weight bytes), far below the 295 ridge, so batch-1 decode is memory-bound. Acceptance test: the caption must not assign both regimes to the same operating point.

As printed the identity is impossible: 'F = 4k+1' with F = 31 fails (31 = 4×7+3), and '1+4(T_j−1) = 31' gives T_j = 8.5. The consistent reading is F = 121 (k = 30), T_j = 31, and '31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames' ✓ — so a single glyph ('31' for '121') corrupts a stated identity. Severity P2 (single-glyph typo), not P1.

The quote is truncated. The checkable requirement is that the HDR series' bandwidth basis (HDR = 200 Gb/s, i.e. half of NDR 400 Gb/s) must match the ring model's byte count and the figure title's promise. Acceptance test: recompute the ring model's bytes from the stated per-hop payload and confirm the labelled basis.

The pull-quote's own pair violates the linearity it states: 2·70B·1,000 = 1.4e14 = 0.14 PFLOP (not 0.28), while 2·70B·32,000 = 4.48e15 = 4.5 PFLOP ✓. So 0.28 → 4.5 is a 16× rise for a 32× rise in L. Under a 4N convention the 1K figure is right and the 32K figure is wrong by 2×; either way the pair is internally inconsistent. Fix: 0.14 PFLOP at 1K → 4.5 PFLOP at 32K. Severity P1 — it is a prominent pull-quote and the error propagates into the reader's model of prefill cost.

35 GB ÷ 50 GB/s (400 Gb/s InfiniBand) = 0.70 s ≈ the caption's 0.8 s, so the caption is self-consistent IF the link is 400 Gb/s IB; the alleged 10× contradiction depends on the figure's own link label (over NVLink at 450 GB/s the transfer is ~0.08 s). Acceptance test: read the link label in the figure and recompute. Separately, reconcile the 35 GB per-request KV with the canonical 24.1 GB (Ch 11) / 24.9 GB (Ch 7) / 27.2 GB (Ch 19): 35 GB implies ~13.4K tokens at 2.62 MB/token, so the figure's context length must be stated.

High priority; the arithmetic framework is sound and the correct value can be supplied. Causal attention FLOPs for a prefill of L tokens = 2·L²·d·n_layers = 2 × (9,200)² × 8,192 × 80 = 1.11e14 FLOP ≈ 0.11 PFLOP (full square 4L²d·n_layers = 0.22 PFLOP), against the linear term 2NL = 1.29 PFLOP — so attention is ~9% (causal) of the linear term at 9.2K and cannot dominate. The crossover where attention = linear is L* = 2N ÷ (160·d) = 106.8K tokens (53.4K for the full square). Acceptance test: recompute the printed substitution against these values.

The verdict conflates per-request latency with aggregate throughput: 9,200 tokens ÷ 19,800 tok/s = 0.465 s, so a single prefill host clears the 1.2 s TTFT budget for ONE request; the failure is aggregate (10 rps × 9,200 = 92,000 tok/s required vs 19,800 available → 4.65 hosts). A verdict cell reading '✗ throughput at a single prefill host' without stating the offered load is numerically false as written. Acceptance test: the verdict must state the offered rate and the budget it is tested against.

Operator error: '92K × 19.8K ≈ 4.65' — 92,000 × 19,800 = 1.82e9, whereas the intended 92,000 ÷ 19,800 = 4.65 ✓. The result is right, the operator is wrong, and it sits in a displayed derivation a reader may copy. Severity P2 (single glyph), not P1.

Unit contradiction on the face of the figure: the y-axis is labelled 'Prefill FLOPs / req (GFLOP)' while the no-cache series is drawn flat at 100 and the caption describes the quantity as a percent of no-cache. A flat-at-100 series cannot be GFLOPs. Acceptance test: one unit on the axis; if the series is a ratio, label it '% of no-cache prefill FLOPs' and give the absolute GFLOP in the caption.

An unqualified 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b)' in the outcome box contradicts Table 12-2's row (b) verdict on the facing page. ONE root cause, two anchors: the figure's claim must carry the same conditions as the table's verdict, and the two must be reconciled in the same edit.

Well-formed: if the headline object (the frozen self-host line at $155,816.93/mo) is not drawn in the plot area, the figure's central comparison is missing and the legend's single swatch is keyed to nothing visible. Acceptance test: the line must be visible, keyed in the legend, and labelled.

Notation defect, wrong severity. '$20.80/K' and '$15–25/K' are ambiguous (per 1K tokens? per 1K requests?) while the note says '$15–25/1K price band'; the house convention fixes decimal-K for tokens, so the figure must read '$20.80 per 1K tokens'. Severity P3, not P1.

The quote is truncated and hedged ('appears to read'), so the defect cannot be pinned. The checkable issue is the VOLUME BASIS: 10 rps × 2,592,000 s = 25.92M req/mo, whereas 6.24M req/mo corresponds to ~2.4 rps — a 4.15× difference. If the canonical workload is 10 rps, a crossover placed at 6.24M req/mo is misplaced by that factor. Acceptance test: state the rps behind 6.24M and reconcile with Ch 4's 10 rps and the 25.92M figure.

The alleged self-contradiction is not one: 'the N = 1 residual (~6 req/s) clears the burst only at ρ = 1 — at ρ = 0.85 it [fails]' is exactly consistent, since 'only at ρ = 1' is what the following clause states.
